requirements_slice.system_goal: Detach WeekBrief assembly from report_workflow private helpers and isolate frontend compatibility reconstruction without changing Week product semantics.

in_scope.item: Extract a Week-owned backend helper module for Week seed bundle assembly, Week day normalization, Week summary normalization, and any Week-owned chunk/block parsing needed by WeekBrief assembly.
Rewire WeekBrief assembly and Week prompt-context preparation to consume the Week-owned helper boundary instead of report_workflow.py private helpers.
Split canonical Week mapping from legacy compatibility reconstruction on the frontend so /week stays canonical-only.
Document the next bounded decomposition seam for report_workflow.py and main.py without performing the full decomposition in this feature.

out_of_scope.item: Changing Week scoring, day semantics, explainability semantics, or payload contracts.
Changing visible Week layouts or adding new Week UI states.

use_case.summary: Maintain Week seed ownership independently from report orchestration internals.
use_case.scenario: week_brief_service.py imports Week-owned seed helpers instead of report_workflow.py private helpers.
Week prompt-context preparation reuses the same Week-owned seed helper module without leaving WeekBrief seed normalization owned by report_workflow.py.
If Week seed data is partial or chunk parsing degrades, existing WeekBrief fallback and telemetry semantics remain stable.

use_case.summary: Keep canonical /week mapping separate from legacy compatibility reconstruction.
use_case.scenario: Canonical /week mapping continues to accept week_brief only and remains fail-closed for non-canonical inputs.
Legacy week_map plus chunk reconstruction lives in an explicit compatibility helper and does not re-enter the canonical product path.
Visible Week states, CTA behavior, and secondary deep-read behavior remain unchanged.

business_invariants.invariant: WeekBrief payload, envelope, status mapping, fallback semantics, and week_brief_* structured events remain unchanged.
report_workflow.py remains a workflow orchestrator and prompt-context owner, not the long-term ownership boundary for WeekBrief seed normalization.
The canonical /week product path maps only week_brief and remains fail-closed for non-canonical inputs.
Legacy week_map or chunk reconstruction remains explicit compatibility behavior and must not become the /week product path.

expected_failure_handling.item: If Week-owned seed data is missing or incomplete, the backend preserves existing WeekBrief fallback and envelope behavior instead of reintroducing direct report_workflow helper imports.
If canonical week_brief is absent on the frontend, /week stays honest and fail-closed rather than reconstructing a substitute product surface from legacy inputs.

If packet-local observability reflects only test-emitted WeekBrief evidence, degraded-but-expected is acceptable only when the verifier states that no dedicated canonical emitter command was intentionally owned by the wave.

known_defects.defect: week_brief_service.py directly depends on Week helper ownership that historically lived in report_workflow.py, which blurs WeekBrief boundaries.
frontend/lib/week-brief.ts historically mixed canonical mapping and compatibility reconstruction, obscuring the canonical /week boundary.
report_workflow.py and main.py remain oversized after this slice; only the next extraction seam is prepared here.

success_criteria.criterion: A Week-owned backend helper module becomes the source of truth for Week seed bundle assembly and Week normalization helpers.
week_brief_service.py no longer imports Week seed helpers directly from report_workflow.py private functions.
Week prompt-context wiring still works after the backend seed-boundary extraction.
Frontend canonical Week mapping and compatibility reconstruction are split into separate helper modules with stable behavior.
Targeted backend, frontend helper, and Week E2E verification passes with an explicit non-blocking packet-local WeekBrief observability verdict.
